newsitem.title: UK: UK power price formula to be hard on shareholders.
newsitem.headline: UK power price formula to be hard on shareholders.

text.p: The RPI minus "x" price-setting formula for the British electricity industry had initially benefitted investors and customers alike, but shareholders now faced "an increasingly tough time ahead," Stephen Littlechild, director general of electricty supply, said on Wednesday.
He said electricity prices for industrial users had fallen 15-20 percent in real terms and they now enjoyed the lowest prices of any major European industrial country.
Domestic users had also seen a 15 percent real-terms price fall, Littlechild told parliament's trade and industry select committee.

Asked about the impact of the main opposition Labour party's proposed windfall tax on the excess profits of privatised utilities, Littlechild acknowledged that companies affected by the tax could ask him to relax his pricing formula as a result.
"I cannot say that was impossible," Littlechild said.

Stressing that he was dealing with hypotheses, he said that even if he were to accept the pleas of utilities affected by the windfall tax, the Trade and Industry Secretary would have the right to veto any licence amendment proposed by the electricty regulator.
